review_method: Checked the Kengo Kuma and Associates project page for exact project identity, Miyagi location, 2022 completion, floor area, program and design authorship.
Used the official portfolio only as identity evidence because its credited professional photography has no stated open reuse license.
Checked the Commons file page and metadata for description, capture date, own-work authorship, dimensions and CC BY-SA 3.0 rights.
Opened both the 5753 by 3835 Commons original and the existing 1600 by 1066 repository derivative and confirmed that both show the completed memorial building.

Queried production read-only and found one existing Kengo Kuma architect, existing cultural and civic-public broad types, existing museum and community-center functions, and no target building or CASE-015 profile conflict.

Selected museum as the only function because the building displays disaster memories and artworks; did not infer the specific community-center function from the official site's broader Community category.

identity_evidence: Kengo Kuma and Associates identifies the completed 2022 Miyagi project as Minamisanriku 311 Memorial, a 1433 square metre two-storey facility designed as the culmination of the town reconstruction plan.
The official description states that disaster memories and artworks are displayed inside, supporting the museum function without inventing a separate memorial taxonomy.

image.visual_evidence: The image clearly shows the completed memorial's torii-like opening and radial Minamisanriku cedar louvers, matching the first-party project description.
